title: A polarity marker negates the operation rather than its result
summary: A narrow polarity model attaches a negative marker to an operation predicate, leaving the input/result description asserted; a result-scoped model instead denies the resulting state.

design.unit: records containing an operation, its input, a result/state field, and one polarity marker
design.contrast: negated operation versus negated result state
design.prediction: With the operation marker present, the input may remain asserted while the operation is absent; a result-scoped marker should preserve the operation but deny the result state.
design.countermodel: A context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial packaging could produce the same surface distribution without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: Matched records show the marker consistently denies the result while the operation remains asserted, or it changes both operation and result with no scope distinction.
design.principal_risk: Independent polarity and event annotations are missing. Related to earlier polarity and action/result routes, but the proposed distinction is attachment target.
